newsitem.title: USA: 3Com says Dec sales weak - analysts.
newsitem.headline: 3Com says Dec sales weak - analysts.

text.p: 3Com Corp executives told analysts Tuesday it had weak sales of its networking products in the last few weeks of December.

At its annual analyst conference in New York, the Santa Clara, Calif.-based maker of computer networking gear suggested sales of its stackable hub -- devices that shuffle information through networks -- were weak, analysts who listened to the conference said.
"There was a lot of concern that they were talking expectations for the quarter down," said Paul Weinstein, analyst at PaineWebber Inc.
"But they also said things picked up again in January."
Eric Benhamou, in a passing reference at the beginning of the conference, said sales of key products were weaker than expected in the second half of December, analysts said.
The comments stoked concerns that had arisen in recent weeks about 3Com's performance.
"The weak sales are not what you would expect given strong sales of personal computers," said Roxane Googin, an analyst at Gruntal & Co.
3Com's products are used to tie together networks of personal computers to share information.
Following Behamou's remarks, 3Com's stock slid 3-1/2 to 61-1/4 on Nasdaq trading of 20 million shares, making the stock the most active in U.S. markets.
3Com officials could not be reached immediately for comment.
